what: Database rule run for «طلب حذف حسابي» (Android_Build_Plan.md A8, MVP_draft.md 64.6): who may ask, who is told and who sees a request (the remove rule of account_remove), withdrawing, the day's limit, removing the account carrying it out and taking what only the person could read

migration.applied: applied to comms-hub (hrghmioxvgkjpnydrxrk) with the owner's approval of 2026-10-28, as version 20261028122912 'account_deletion'; md5 of the stored statement 8ed2dba138462f0c073630ced82970af equals the md5 of the file

how: Each run is one transaction against comms-hub, rolled back at the end, through the MCP execute_sql tool. Seven throwaway accounts (@t.test) act through row level security. The real administrators may remove a throwaway account, so they are told too inside the run; the checks of who is told read the throwaway accounts only. The TOTAL row carries the md5 of the text the run executed, matched below to the file.

runs.text: the migration's statements, then the rule file's, without their comment lines and without the TOTAL row's md5
runs.result: stopped at setup, before any check: the second throwaway administrator was not a founder, and accounts has the check admin_role_is_protected (every administrator is protected). The file was corrected: both throwaway administrators are founders. No database behaviour changed.

after: Checked directly after the last run: 0 requests, 0 throwaway accounts, 0 throwaway sign-ins, 0 throwaway notices, the 5 real accounts untouched; triggers on accounts: accounts_deletion_done, accounts_protect_founders, accounts_revoke_sign_in; row level security on account_deletions; execute on account_deletion_request, account_deletion_withdraw and deletion_visible for authenticated only, on deletion_carriers and account_deletion_done for no client role.

advisors.security: Read in full before and after applying (141,436 and 142,735 characters). Exactly 3 new notices, all authenticated_security_definer_function_executable (WARN) for the functions meant for signed-in people: account_deletion_request, account_deletion_withdraw, and deletion_visible (the read policy's helper, which tells the caller only whether they may see a given person's request). No new notice for anon, none removed. Totals after: 283 authenticated and 21 anon definer notices, 13 rls_enabled_no_policy, 1 leaked password protection; the last three as before.
advisors.performance: Identical before and after: 7 unindexed foreign keys, 25 unused indexes, 2 multiple permissive policies, 1 Auth connection strategy; nothing about account_deletions.

not_rerun: Other rule files were not re-run: no existing function was replaced. The one change to existing behaviour is the trigger accounts_deletion_done on deleting an account, which does nothing without an open request; check 23 covers a removal without a request.
